source_text: Solem quoque esse Christum cunctis timentibus eum Malachias propheta testatur et promittit dicens: uobis autem timentibus meum nomen orietur sol iustitiae, et sanitas in alis eius, ostendens ex nullo nobis salutem posse conferri, nisi in passionem crucis eius, qua extendens manus cuncta saeculi saluaturus amplexus est, conuerso ad eum timore credamus et ad aeternitatem uitae spe futuri regni eius animemur. quis ergo tam stolidus ac demens, quis sic ab intellectu suae salutis alienus, qui in tot et tantis testimoniis ueritatis incredulus non aduersus sinceram fidem obduratum pectus intellectu ueritatis emolliat et e tenebris uitae quondam mortalis exutos in lumine praeceptorum caelestium gradiens ad diuina monita et Domini salutaria gerenda mandata inluminato corde tota mentis credulitate conuertat, ut quem prophetae praedicauerunt Dominum noscat, ut Christum qui se mundo palam uenisse monstrauit intellegat, ut scripturis diuinitus testificantibus Dei filium et Deum credat. sicut ipse quae sit uita aeterna manifestat dicens: haec est autem uita aeterna, ut cognoscant te solum et uerum Deum et quem misisti Iesum Christum, docens atque ostendens nihil aliud esse Deum nosse quam credere et oculos cordis in Dominum prona et immutata pectoris fide deuotae mentis aperire. inde iam fit ut credendo intellegas, intellegendo quod credis in sensu Deum illuminato corde conspicias, sicut idem ipse Dominus et per Esaiam ante monet dicens: si non credideritis, nec intellegetis. tam facilis et praestans et larga est atque abundans de Domini pietate clementia, ut si quis semel sese in eum toto timore conuerterit ad caeleste munus admissus statim iam eius non nisi ad diuina mens pateat et ad caelum ac superna oculos cordis attollens Christi lumen partae iam salutis aspiciat.
thought_title: Christ as the Sun of Righteousness and the Call to Believe
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius, arguing that the prophets foretold Christ as the sun of righteousness and that unbelief is a willful refusal to turn to the light of salvation.
pass_a_gloss: Malachi the prophet testifies and promises that Christ is also the sun to all who fear him, saying: 'But for you who fear my name the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in his wings,' showing that salvation can be conferred on us from nothing, unless we believe in the passion of his cross, by which, stretching out his hands, he embraced all things of the world to save them, with fear turned toward him, and unless we are stirred to the eternity of life by the hope of his future kingdom. Who therefore is so stupid and mad, who is so alien from the understanding of his own salvation, who, being unbelieving in so many and so great testimonies of the truth, would not soften his hardened breast against sincere faith by the understanding of the truth, and, stripped from the darkness of a formerly mortal life, walking in the light of heavenly precepts, would not turn with an illuminated heart and with the whole faith of his mind to the divine warnings and to the carrying out of the Lord's saving commands, so that he may know the Lord whom the prophets preached, so that he may understand Christ, who showed that he had come openly to the world, so that he may believe the Son of God and God, with the scriptures testifying divinely. Just as he himself reveals what eternal life is, saying: 'But this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent,' teaching and showing that to know God is nothing other than to believe and to open the eyes of the heart to the Lord with the ready and unchangeable faith of the breast of a devoted mind. Thence it now happens that by believing you may understand, by understanding what you believe you may see God in your perception with an illuminated heart, just as the same Lord himself also warns beforehand through Isaiah, saying: 'If you will not believe, you will not understand.' So easy and excellent and generous and abundant is the mercy from the Lord's piety, that if anyone once turns himself to him with all fear, admitted to the heavenly gift, immediately his mind is open to nothing but divine things, and, lifting the eyes of his heart to heaven and the things above, he may look upon the light of Christ of the salvation already obtained.

choices.why: The glossary requires this exact rendering for the Malachi citation.
Literal rendering of the Old Latin wording, preserving the physical image of wings.
The glossary bans 'disbelief' and 'incredulity' for incredulitas; the adjective is rendered consistently as 'unbelieving'.
The glossary requires 'fear' for timor, preserving the reverent fear of God.
The glossary requires 'faith' for credulitas, avoiding 'belief' and 'credulity'.
The glossary requires 'salvation' for salus, avoiding 'deliverance' and 'safety'.

pass_b_english: The prophet Malachi also testifies and promises that Christ is the sun for all who fear him, saying: "But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing is in his wings" (Malachi 4:2). He shows that salvation can be brought to us from no other source than the passion of his cross, by which he stretched out his hands and embraced all the world to save it. We are to believe by turning our fear toward him, and we are stirred toward the eternity of life by hope in his coming kingdom. Who, then, is so stupid and insane, who is so far removed from understanding his own salvation, that he remains unbelieving amid so many and such great testimonies to the truth, and does not soften his hardened heart against sincere faith by understanding the truth? Who does not, stripped from the darkness of what was once a mortal life and walking in the light of the heavenly commandments, turn with an enlightened heart and the whole faith of his mind to the divine warnings and the saving commands of the Lord to carry them out? Who does not come to know the Lord whom the prophets proclaimed, to understand the Christ who showed plainly that he had come into the world, to believe that he is the Son of God and God, as the Scriptures testify by divine authority? Christ himself reveals what eternal life is, saying: "Now this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent" (John 17:3). He teaches and shows that knowing God is nothing other than believing, and opening the eyes of the heart to the Lord with a devoted mind's faith, fixed and unwavering in the heart. From this it now comes about that by believing you understand, and by understanding what you believe you see God in your mind with an enlightened heart. The Lord himself also warns of this beforehand through Isaiah, saying: "If you will not believe, you will not understand" (Isaiah 7:9). So easy, so excellent, so generous and abundant is the mercy that flows from the Lord's goodness, that if anyone once turns himself to him with complete fear, he is admitted to the heavenly gift, and from that moment his mind is open to nothing but divine things. Lifting the eyes of his heart to heaven and the heights, he looks upon the light of Christ, the salvation he has now obtained.
